findings.title: os.replace makes destination inherit mkstemp's 0600 mode, discarding existing permissions
findings.evidence: The temp file created by 'tempfile.mkstemp(' is mode 0600 regardless of umask, and 'os.replace(tmp_path, path)' moves that inode over the destination, so after the first save the state file is always 0600 and owned by the writer - any existing 0644/0660 mode granted to a companion process or group is silently lost and that reader will start failing with PermissionError.
findings.recommendation: Stat the existing destination before writing and chmod/chown the temp file to match (or apply an explicit, documented mode such as 0o644) just before os.replace; document the chosen policy in the docstring.

findings.title: Unguarded directory fsync after rename raises on filesystems without dir-fsync support
findings.evidence: 'os.fsync(dir_fd)' is called outside the try/except and after os.replace has already committed the new file, so on filesystems that reject fsync on a directory fd (EINVAL/EBADF, some network/FUSE mounts) save_state raises although the state was written - a caller that retries or reports failure now disagrees with the actual on-disk state.
findings.recommendation: Tolerate errno.EINVAL/EBADF/ENOTSUP from the directory fsync (log or ignore) so durability best-effort failures do not mask a completed write, and open with os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY to avoid fsyncing a non-directory after a concurrent replacement.

findings.title: Saving through a symlinked path replaces the symlink instead of its target
findings.evidence: 'os.replace(tmp_path, path)' renames onto the path itself; if the deployment points path at a symlink (e.g. /var/lib/app/state.json -> /data/state.json), the link is replaced by a regular file and the real target is left stale, so readers of the target silently observe old state.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the destination with os.path.realpath(path) before computing the directory and calling os.replace, or reject/ignore symlinked destinations explicitly and document the behaviour.
